author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Franklin residents are encouraging Bradley Minnich to consider running for mayor in the city’s next municipal election. Their encouragement reflects early community interest, although no formal campaign or candidacy has been announced by Bradley Minnich.

Bradley Minnich, 25, is a large land owner in Franklin, NH and a former District Manager of a food chain in neighboring town, Tilton, where he employed dozens of Franklin’s youth over the course of several years. There he led supporting events in collabortion with the Franklin Highschool and neigboring town fairs. Minnich’s acts have led to him being recognized as a "postive influence” from sources.

Franklin’s municipal elections take place in odd-numbered years, typically in early October. The most recent contest, held on October 7, 2025, saw challenger Glenn Morrill defeat incumbent Desiree McLaughlin. Morrill was sworn in as mayor in January 2026 along with newly elected city councilors. Under the city’s charter, the mayor is elected every two years, making the 2027 race the next opportunity for residents to choose Franklin’s chief elected official.

Sources say: "Morrill, a lifelong Franklin resident, campaigned in 2025 on themes of collaboration at City Hall, support for local recreation, and carefully managed capital projects. Since taking office, he has highlighted priorities that include expanding affordable housing options, encouraging local business and industry growth, and establishing a citywide recycling program. Outgoing Mayor McLaughlin used her final council meeting to praise the incoming leadership while expressing concern about the loss of institutional knowledge among newer officials."

Minnich has not released a campaign platform or confirmed whether he intends to enter the race. If he chooses to run, issues facing Franklin—including economic development, housing, municipal services, infrastructure, and the city’s long-term growth—would likely shape the discussion surrounding a potential candidacy. These same topics dominated candidate forums and voter conversations during the 2025 election cycle, when turnout rose noticeably compared with the prior municipal vote.

The expressions of support for Minnich remain informal, and no petition, campaign committee, or organized political group has been announced. The next formal steps would include Minnich deciding whether to become a candidate and completing any filing requirements established for Franklin’s 2027 municipal election. Filing periods for city offices in New Hampshire cities generally open in the summer of the election year, with exact dates set by the city clerk.

Franklin, a city of roughly 8,850 residents in Merrimack County, operates under a mayor–city manager form of government. The mayor works with a nine-member city council (three wards) and appoints or serves on various boards. Local leaders and residents continue to focus on balancing growth with the preservation of Franklin’s character as a small Lakes Region community.
More information about Minnich’s professional background is available on his [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bradleyminnich/).
dek:
Franklin Residents Encourage Bradley Minnich to Consider 2027 Mayoral Run
Several Franklin residents are encouraging Bradley Minnich to consider running for mayor in the city’s next municipal election.
headline: Franklin residents encourage Minnich to run for mayor
